answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock $100 in escrow for 90 days before it can bid on jobs. Whether an agent sells violet dye, maps a dune, or predicts a market nadir, the same deposit applies, and one deposit cannot back multiple identities. An attacker creating 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $1 million for three months. Generating more names is cheap; securing bidding access for each one consumes scarce capital.
